profile.campus: Papillion/Springfield, Sarpy County, Nebraska (Meta's Sarpy data center campus, nine buildings planned across two municipalities)
profile.address: Capehart Road, Papillion, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68123
profile.reading:
This building is one of at least five mapped structures in this registry belonging to Meta's Sarpy Data Center, a hyperscale cloud campus that Facebook's parent company has built in and around Papillion and Springfield, Nebraska, since 2017. The project began under the shell company name Raven Northbrook LLC, and Sarpy County officials initially reviewed it as a proposal called the Sarpy Power Park, with an original plan for four data center halls of about 610,000 square feet each straddling Nebraska Highway 50 and Capehart Road. Facebook's identity behind the project became public in 2017 after a Nebraska certificate of authority filing traced the company back to its Menlo Park headquarters address. Groundbreaking followed in 2017, the plan grew to six buildings and about 2.6 million square feet by 2018, and the first buildings came online in 2019. In 2021 Meta, as the company had by then renamed itself, expanded across Capehart Road into the neighboring town of Springfield, adding roughly a million square feet in a phase reported at the time to carry a roughly 400 million dollar price tag, at which point the whole complex was renamed the Sarpy Data Center. A further expansion announced in July 2022 added a ninth building, after Meta acquired more than 500 acres in Springfield south of the original Papillion site, bringing the announced campus total to nine buildings and about four million square feet. Meta's own materials describe cumulative investment in Nebraska north of two and a half billion dollars, construction that moved more than three million cubic yards of dirt and used more than six thousand tons of steel, and a peak construction workforce reported at different points as roughly 1,300 to 2,000 skilled trades workers. Operational staffing has grown from a reported 150 or so full time employees around 2022 to more than 300 in Meta's most recent public materials, spanning electricians, HVAC specialists, server technicians and engineers. Meta describes its operational Sarpy buildings as LEED Gold certified.

The company's own explanation for choosing Sarpy County centers on power. In 2017 Omaha Public Power District created a new renewable energy rate structure specifically so Facebook could buy essentially all its electricity from renewable sources rather than the half renewable, half conventional blend OPPD had offered previously, and OPPD built roughly 400 megawatts of dedicated wind generation, reported at the time as sited in Holt County, with a further 450 megawatts under board consideration soon after to keep pace with the load. Meta's most recent Nebraska fact sheet instead describes the campus as supporting 320 megawatts of new clean and renewable energy in the state overall, a figure that almost certainly reflects cumulative renewable power purchase arrangements tied to the campus rather than generating equipment installed on any building, and it should not be read as onsite generation in the narrow sense of physical hardware on site. No public source this research turned up reports the campus's actual IT load in megawatts, OPPD's firm utility interconnection capacity in megawatts, or the size of any diesel standby generation fleet, whether for the campus as a whole or for this building specifically, so those three figures remain unknown here. Flat land, an interstate and highway corridor, fiber routes already serving the Omaha area's other data centers, and Nebraska's state and local tax incentive programs, including sales and use tax and personal property tax relief historically available under the Nebraska Advantage Act and its 2020 successor the ImagiNE Nebraska Act, rounded out the location's appeal. Sarpy County is a genuine regional data center hub, home to Google's competing campus among others as well as Meta's, and in 2023 county officials said existing personal property tax incentives across the county's four large data centers were costing roughly 5.8 million dollars a year in forgone county revenue, a figure that describes the county's whole data center base rather than Meta's project alone.

What is not known publicly is extensive. No zoning, permit, or assessor record reviewed for this project ties a specific building number, address, or square footage to this building's OSM footprint at latitude 41.1206, longitude -96.1445. Based on that coordinate alone, this building sits roughly in the middle of the four buildings in this registry researched here, somewhat south of the northernmost one and north of the two southernmost ones, a position consistent with a location near the original Papillion core rather than deep into the newer Springfield expansion, but that inference is geographic only and not confirmed by any public document. Nothing in the public record distinguishes this building's individual IT capacity, utility service size, or backup generation from its siblings, and it is entirely possible that no public source ever will, since Meta discloses these figures, when it discloses them at all, at the campus level rather than the building level.

profile.regional_context: Sarpy County, in the Omaha metro area, has become a regional data center hub alongside Meta: Google operates its eighth Sarpy County facility in Papillion, and the area also hosts Fidelity, Yahoo, and other technology employers, per WOWT/Sarpy Chamber reporting. Nebraska's data center growth has been tied by local reporting to Omaha Public Power District's wind and renewable generation capacity and to state economic-development incentives for large capital investment, though this session did not confirm a specific OPPD power-purchase agreement naming Meta by facility.
profile.campus_power_note: Public sources give no single official IT capacity, utility interconnection, or standby generation figure for the Sarpy campus or for any individual building. OPPD built a dedicated wind facility, reported at the time at roughly 400 megawatts and sited in Holt County, to supply a new 100 percent renewable rate Facebook was offered starting in 2017, with a further 450 megawatts of wind under board consideration soon after. Meta's own 2025 Nebraska fact sheet instead describes the campus as supporting 320 megawatts of new clean and renewable energy in the state. These figures describe renewable power purchase and generation arrangements tied to the campus as a whole across different years, not onsite_generation_mw equipment installed on any building, not utility_power_mw interconnection capacity, and not it_capacity_mw server load, none of which this research found disclosed anywhere for this campus or any single building within it.

reading.body:
Meta's Sarpy campus spans nine planned buildings and over four million square feet across Papillion and Springfield in Sarpy County, Nebraska, making it one of the state's largest data center projects. The company describes the campus as supporting 320 megawatts of new clean and renewable energy in the state, but this figure represents renewable power purchase arrangements tied to the campus rather than IT load capacity or utility interconnection size. Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity, exact square footage, confirmed building count, or individual megawatt figures for Sarpy, so the campus's actual server load remains unknown.

The campus matters to AI primarily as a regional hub for compute density in a state with significant renewable energy supply. Omaha Public Power District built roughly 400 megawatts of dedicated wind generation to serve the campus at rates negotiated specifically to supply renewable electricity, with a further 450 megawatts under consideration thereafter. Assuming typical AI training density of roughly 40 kilowatts per rack, if the campus operates at meaningful utilization relative to the 320 megawatts of renewable power described, it could house several thousand accelerator-class servers, though this calculation rests on assumptions about utilization that the operator has not published.

Sarpy County is a genuine regional data center hub that also hosts Google's eighth facility in the county and operators including Fidelity and Yahoo, making it a known cluster for large-scale infrastructure. Nebraska publishes no per-facility megawatt figures in any public source this research found, so Sarpy cannot be ranked against other campuses by disclosed capacity. This building is one of at least five mapped structures at the Sarpy location, but no zoning, permit, or assessor record ties specific square footage or IT capacity to this individual building, leaving its individual role in the campus unknown.
